newsitem.title: UK: NatWest dips amid stock surplus.
newsitem.headline: NatWest dips amid stock surplus.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc dipped 7-1/2 pence on Monday, defying gains elsewhere in the market and the bank sector, amid an excess of stock in the market, traders said.
Dealers said the stock was unlikely to have been affected by news that banking union Bifu was asking its members to vote in favour of a half-day strike on Christmas eve.
"I'm putting it down to there being simply a lot of stock around. There are no downgrades in the system and I shouldn't think it's the strike," said one market maker.
By 1232 GMT NatWest was down 7-1/2 pence at 671p, trailing the 11-1/2p gain in Barclays shares to 1013-1/2p and the 8-1/2p jump in HSBC Holdings Plc to 12.87-1/2 stg.
Bank stocks mostly rebounded after being among the biggest losers in Friday's market tumble which saw the FTSE 100 record its biggest one-day percent loss in over two years.

"Banks are highly geared to these big market movements," said another trader, pointing out that NatWest could be particularly vulnerable to a downturn in the investment banking business following its recent acquisitions.
Bifu said earlier staff at Lloyds TSB and NatWest were being asked to vote in favour of a half-day strike on Christmas Eve. The union said more than 35,000 staff at the two banks would be balloted.
